html:
SMTO-DB-0006 — SMTO couldn't understand the database query

GUID: 415c8b75-798b-4533-bb33-0bf123cc9cec
Slug: sql-statement-invalid
Domain: DB · Subsystem: db

What happened

  • The database query was empty, had a mistake in how it was written, or contained more than one query at once. SMTO stopped before sending it, so nothing was run on your database.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the Task is still running, wait. SMTO usually rewrites the query and tries again on its own. The error tells SMTO exactly what was wrong with how the query was written.
  2. If you typed the query yourself, send only one query per message and check that nothing is cut off at the end. SMTO accepts exactly one complete query at a time, to keep each step clear and safe.
  3. If it keeps failing, ask SMTO to split your request into smaller questions, for example one table at a time. Simpler queries are easier for SMTO to write correctly.

What success looks like

  • SMTO runs the query and shows the results.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the query you wanted, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep sending the same query unchanged; it will be refused the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The SQL parser could not validate exactly one PostgreSQL statement: the SQL was empty, failed to parse, contained multiple statements, or used a JOIN without a FROM source.

What this means

  • Parsing receives empty SQL, fails to construct a valid PostgreSQL syntax tree, sees multiple statements, or finds a JOIN without its required FROM source. Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.

Why this can happen

  • Parsing receives empty SQL, fails to construct a valid PostgreSQL syntax tree, sees multiple statements, or finds a JOIN without its required FROM source.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect parse_failed/multiple_statements/join syntax evidence while keeping bound values out of public diagnostics.

How to fix it

  • Submit exactly one complete PostgreSQL statement per database.execute call, with no trailing second statement. The parser error in Technical details names the failing token. For join_without_from_source, move generated buckets, VALUES, function calls or subqueries into a WITH CTE, a derived table or the FROM clause before joining. Keep parameter binding intact and inspect the target before any write.
  • Correct the SQL syntax and submit one statement per operation. Preserve parameter binding and inspect the target database before any mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • One supported statement parses and passes classification without silently dropping SQL.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
